title: PRD: Hosted Inference Endpoint Contracts (MVP) and Progressive Launch Checklist
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Background:
Redwood's hosted API is converging multiple inference surfaces (chat, completion, embeddings, rerank) into a consistent, production-grade contract for customers. This PRD defines the minimal behavioral contracts for the MVP hosted endpoints, clarifies scope for the initial launch, and provides a progressive launch checklist to reduce risk for high-traffic customers.

Goals:
- Define unambiguous behavioral contracts (inputs, outputs, error modes) for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank that are stable for the hosted product launch.
- Provide acceptance criteria and test harnesses to prevent regressions across model swaps and runtime optimizations.
- Outline a progressive rollout/runbook that supports canary traffic slices, automated regressions detection, and safe rollback.

Non-goals:
- Full feature parity with Dedicated (reserved capacity) in the first launch phase.
- Deep SDK ergonomics (will iterate post-launch).

Scope Clarifications (decisions):
- Chat vs Completions: chat endpoint will enforce message schema and role fields; completions will accept a prompt string or array and return a single completion object. Both will share streaming and tool-calling contracts.
- Embeddings: return deterministic float vectors for the same model+input at same runtime config; minor numerical variance OK across quantized model variants if within tolerance.
- Rerank: accept a ranked list of candidate documents + query; return stable ordering and scores normalized to 0-1.
- Rate limits: initial tiered limits will mirror the existing hosted product tiers; throttling responses must use 429 with Retry-After header.

API Surface (MVP summary):
- /v1/chat: POST {messages: [{role, content, metadata?}], model, max_tokens, stream?} -> {id, choices: [{message, finish_reason}], usage} or stream SSE of choices.
- /v1/completions: POST {prompt, model, n, max_tokens, temperature, stream?} -> {id, choices, usage}.
- /v1/embeddings: POST {input: string|[string], model} -> {data: [{embedding, index}], model}.
- /v1/rerank: POST {query, candidates: [{id, text}], model} -> {ranked: [{id, score}], explanation?}.

Operational Contracts:
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms for small models; 95th percentile response time for embeddings <= 200ms in hosted region during steady state.
- Availability: targeted SLA 99.9% for launched lanes; initial GA will be best-effort with documented fallback.
- Error semantics: client errors 4xx, server errors 5xx; transient errors should surface 503 + Retry-After when degraded.

Acceptance Criteria (high level):
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral: Endpoints return responses that match schema for 99.9% of requests in synthetic test harness across traffic profiles.
Quality: No regression in quality metrics (LLM eval suites) above defined thresholds when routing between model variants during rollout.
Reliability: Canary traffic (1%) for 72h shows error rate <= baseline + 0.5% and latencies within SLOs before increasing traffic slice.
Observability: Token-level cost, latency breakdown, and per-route tracing are enabled and visible in Console for launched endpoints.
Security: KMS integration for customer data in transit at rest confirmed for hosted lane; security review completed.
Compatibility: SDKs validate those endpoints and include streaming and non-streaming code paths with automatic reconnect/resume tests.
Docs: Public API docs and behavioral contract page published prior to first canary and linked in the Console onboarding flow.
rollout_checklist: Pre-launch: Complete security review and threat model (tickets: SEC-2171, SEC-2203)
Pre-launch: Smoke end-to-end tests (chat->model->stream->console) passing in staging with synthetic load
Canary 1 (1% traffic, 24h): Monitor errors, p99 latency, quality drift; hold if metrics exceed thresholds
Canary 2 (10% traffic, 48h): Expand traffic, run replay tests against production traffic sample; validate cost telemetry
Gradual ramp (25%, 50%, 100%): At each step run automated evals, customer-facing tests, and manual sign-off from PM/Eng/SRE
Rollback plan: Automated traffic cut to previous stable model pool and activate degraded-mode fallback endpoints (read-only)
test_plan: Contract tests: Schema validators for all endpoints with fuzz inputs and property-based tests
Load tests: Simulated multi-tenant traffic profiles to validate autoscaling and latency SLOs
Quality tests: Regression evals with golden prompt sets for chat/completion/embeddings/rerank
Chaos: Inject network partitions and GPU OOM in staging to validate graceful degradation and fallbacks
Integration: SDK conformance tests including streaming reconnect, partial tokens, and Retry-After handling
metrics: Per-route token cost and aggregate cust bill estimates
Quality drift: evaluation score deltas on golden prompt suites
Canary signal composite score (latency, error rate, eval drift)
open_questions: Should rerank include an optional explanation payload in MVP or behind feature flag?
Tolerance bounds for numerical variance in embeddings across quantized backends (proposal: cosine delta < 0.002)
Exact rate limit tiers for free vs paid customers (finance input required)
